content.text:
Confirmed: I clobbered the AUDIT_LEDGER — S1942/S1960 entries are gone. The file went from (probably ~722 lines, larger) to 53817 bytes / 432 lines. The read must have returned only part of the file (perhaps a byte cap ~50KB?). So `tools.read` returned truncated content, and I wrote that back, losing history.

Recovery: git has the file tracked (modified). I can restore the committed version and re-append my entry. But careful: the committed version may be older than the current (pre-my-edit) version if other agents appended entries without committing. Let me check `git diff --stat` and see what the committed version looks like: `git show HEAD:AUDIT_LEDGER.md` size/lines and whether it contains S1942/S1960. If HEAD's version contains all the entries (i.e., nothing uncommitted was lost except my edit), restoring is safe.

Let me check:
- `git show HEAD:AUDIT_LEDGER.md | Measure-Object` line count.
- Compare with what we know: the pre-edit file had ~722 lines per my earlier count and contained S1942, S1960 entries.

If HEAD's ledger has ~722+ lines and contains S1942/S1960, then simply restore and re-append my entry (using a safer append method that doesn't rely on tools.read of the whole file).

Safer append method: use PowerShell `Add-Content` with a here-string written via a temp file... Still quoting issues. Alternative: use Node fs in run_code! I can use the tool `pwsh` or better: Node's `fs` via `await import("fs")` — the run_code environment has Node APIs available. That's the cleanest: `fs.appendFileSync(path, text)`. But the text must be in the program as a string — same template literal constraints, fine (my entry has no backticks).

Even better: use `fs.readFileSync` + `fs.writeFileSync` with full content in Node — but I need to be careful about encoding (UTF-8) — the tools write probably handles UTF-8 fine.

Plan:
1. `git diff` for AUDIT_LEDGER.md to see exactly what my write changed relative to HEAD (deleted lines etc.).
2. Restore HEAD version via `git checkout -- AUDIT_LEDGER.md` — but only if HEAD contains all the content that existed before my edit (need to verify: does HEAD contain the S1942 entry? and S1960?). If HEAD is missing entries that existed only in the working tree (uncommitted), restoring would lose them. Let me check `git diff` to see if the diff includes deletions of entries that were in HEAD (meaning my write deleted them) vs. additions.

Specifically: `git diff --numstat` and check whether HEAD's file is ~53KB+ or larger. If HEAD's version is LARGER (contains the deleted entries), then my write deleted content that was committed, so restoring is perfect.

Let me check.

content.name: run_code
content.arguments:
{"code": "const cmd = `
$ErrorActionPreference='Continue'
Write-Output '--- HEAD version stats ---'
$h = git -C D:\\lean show HEAD:AUDIT_LEDGER.md
Write-Output ('HEAD_lines=' + ($h | Measure-Object).Count)
$tmp = 'D:\\lean\\tmp\\_head_ledger.md'
git -C D:\\lean show HEAD:AUDIT_LEDGER.md | Set-Content -Path $tmp -Encoding utf8
Write-Output ('HEAD_bytes=' + (Get-Item $tmp).Length)
Write-Output ('HEAD_has_S1942=' + ((Select-String -Path $tmp -Pattern 'S1942PrePsiFive' -SimpleMatch | Measure-Object).Count))
Write-Output ('HEAD_has_S1960=' + ((Select-String -Path $tmp -Pattern 'S1960' -SimpleMatch | Measure-Object).Count))
Write-Output ('HEAD_has_S1977=' + ((Select-String -Path $tmp -Pattern 'S1977' -SimpleMatch | Measure-Object).Count))
Write-Output '--- diff numstat for worktree ledger ---'
git -C D:\\lean diff --numstat -- AUDIT_LEDGER.md
Write-Output '--- diff of last part (what I removed) : deleted-line signature ---'
git -C D:\\lean diff -- AUDIT_LEDGER.md | Select-String -Pattern '^-## ' | Select-Object -First 20 | ForEach-Object { $_.Line }
`;
const r = await tools.pwsh({ description: "Compare HEAD ledger with worktree", command: cmd, workdir: "D:\\lean", timeoutMs: 120000 });
console.log(r.kind==="foreground" ? r.stdout.text + "\n[stderr]\n" + r.stderr.text : JSON.stringify(r));
", "description": "Compare HEAD ledger with current worktree version"}
